bullets.title: July Retail Sales Miss Consensus; But Consumer Trend Intact
bullets.body: Headline retail sales fell 0.6% m/m (control group -0.4%) vs. consensus for +0.1% and +0.4% respectively, the softest print since May 2025. Multiple sources attribute the bulk of the weakness to Amazon Prime Day shifting from July to June (non-store sales -2.2% m/m), with credit card data accelerating late July into August. 3Q real PCE tracking ~1.8-2.25%, income growth remains supportive, and the underlying consumer trend is characterized as solid at +3% q/q annualized.

bullets.title: Fed Rate Hike Pushed Fully to 2027; Financial Conditions at Most Accommodative Since 1990s
bullets.body: Following soft July PPI and retail data, markets have pushed next Fed hike pricing to 2027, with September probability below 33%. Bloomberg's US Financial Conditions index has loosened to its most accommodative level since the 1990s. Core PCE ex-financial services tracking only ~10bps in July (3-month annualized 2.06%), reducing urgency for near-term tightening.

bullets.title: Yield Curve Steepens to Cycle High; 30Y Auction Clears at 25-Year High
bullets.body: The 10s2s yield curve widened to +51-52bps, a new cycle high, with 10-year yields at ~4.65-4.66%. The 30-year Treasury auction cleared at 5.126-5.22% (sources vary slightly), the highest long-term borrowing cost in 25 years, with foreign participation pulling back from July levels. Morgan Stanley favors 7s30s steepeners and sees 10-year yields potentially declining toward 4.3%.

bullets.title: SPY at All-Time Highs; Russell 2000 Outperforming on Quad Shift
bullets.body: 8 of 11 S&P sectors are green, pushing SPY to all-time highs in what Hedgeye characterizes as a textbook quad shift pattern. Russell 2000 is up 23% YTD, outperforming S&P 500 by 9.1%, with Q2 earnings beating by 4.4% above expectations. S&P 500 profit margins are at all-time recorded highs; Citi raised 2026 S&P 500 EPS estimate to $365.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Multi-Year Capex Cycle Intact; ~40 GW Grid Shortfall Looms Through 2028
bullets.body: Hyperscaler capex expectations exceed $1T in 2027; Stephen Byrd (Morgan Stanley) published FT op-ed projecting ~40 GW grid access shortfall for US data center developers through 2028, with fuel cells and energy storage identified as AI power enablers. Anthropic signed a 20-year, $9.1B lease with Riot Platforms for 191MW at Rockdale, and is targeting 10GW of compute online via Macquarie/GIC partnerships. Fermi signed a 15-year deal for 222MW (expandable to 650MW) with TensorWave generating ~$6.5B contracted revenue starting 2H27.

bullets.title: Semis Best Month Since 2003; Memory Leading Recovery with Structural Demand Inflection
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks are up 10%+ in August, on pace for their best month since 2003. Memory stocks lead the recovery with SNDK surging ~14-25% after committing to 100% excess cash return and flagging NAND TAM inflecting from ~$70B in CY25 to $300B+ in CY26 and $500B+ in CY27. JPMorgan estimates SNDK industry wafer capacity is ~30% below prior peak at ~100% utilization with allocation constraints visible beyond CY27. DRAM alone is projected to generate ~$1T in revenue in 2027, matching cumulative 2010-2025 total.

bullets.title: AI Model Pricing Wars Intensify; OpenAI Surpasses $40B ARR
bullets.body: OpenAI's annualized revenue run rate topped $40B in July, roughly doubling from year-end 2025. Simultaneously, OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna pricing 80%, Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5 at half prior price, and Google unveiled Gemini 3.7 Flash with a 50% pricing cut — leading US model prices down ~25% since mid-July. Chinese AI competition is cited as a key driver of the price war.

bullets.title: AMAT Beats and Raises But Sells Off on High Expectations; WFE Cycle Still Extending
bullets.body: Applied Materials guided F4Q to $10.25B (vs. ~$9.60B consensus), with Semi Systems segment qualitatively raised above the prior 30%+ Y/Y growth framework. Largest customers are now providing 8-quarter demand forecasts extending roadmap discussions to 2030; CY27 expected to be another record WFE growth year. Despite the beat, AMAT sold off ~6% as elevated positioning and flat q/q near-term gross margin created a 'show-me' dynamic. UBS sees AMAT path to ~$30 EPS with ~200bps share gains.

bullets.title: VIX Term Structure Steep; Single-Stock Vol Compressed to Median Levels
bullets.body: Short-dated pre-FOMC/Jackson Hole VIX has been crushed while longer-dated vol (3+ months) holds a bid, creating steep term structure. VIXEQ (single-stock vol) is down 13 points from >50 in late July to ~37, now at median historical levels. Skew has flattened to the 4th percentile as investors added upside calls on the recent rebound, with the biggest compression in Semis and Tech Hardware — creating overwrite/risk-reversal opportunities per MS derivatives desk.

bullets.title: US-Iran Tensions Escalate; Strait of Hormuz Tanker Strike and Indefinite Blockade Threat
bullets.body: The US stated it could maintain a naval blockade of Iran indefinitely with plans to increase economic pressure on Tehran amid failed ceasefire talks. The IRGC struck an oil tanker with a drone in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude is up ~0.7-1% to ~$88/bbl; Saudi oil tankers are increasingly going dark due to Houthi blockade, and diesel crack spreads have hit all-time highs.

bullets.title: PBOC Makes Historic Mid-Month Liquidity Injection of $52B
bullets.body: The People's Bank of China injected 348 billion yuan (~$52B) via overnight reverse repos — characterized as the first mid-month injection of this kind in PBOC history. China Jan-July new yuan loans came in at CNY10.38T vs. CNY10.62T estimated, signaling weaker-than-expected credit growth. Taiwan, meanwhile, is tracking double-digit GDP growth for the first time since 2010, with Korean chipmakers surging on AI demand.

bullets.title: Dispersion Index Falling as AI FOMO Pulls Back; Software and Financials Still Outperform
bullets.body: The CBOE Dispersion Index (DSPX) is declining sharply as AI enthusiasm fades and crowded bullish trades deleverage. Non-TMT long/short funds are buying memory stocks at ~2.3x the rate of TMT-focused funds. Software and Financials continue to outperform while AI-FOMO names see position unwinds.

bullets.title: Goldman Raises European Equity Targets; UK GDP Beats in June
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs raised its FTSE 100 12-month forecast to 11,400 (from prior) and its STOXX 600 target to 695 from 660. UK Q2 GDP grew 1.7% annualized (0.4% q/q), beating expectations, with June showing +0.3% m/m driven by services. REC survey shows permanent job placements at 50.0 in July, the highest in nearly four years, though Q3 growth is forecast to slow to 0.8% annualized.

bullets.title: 10-Year Treasury at 4.65%; Rates Repricing Financials and Steepener Trades
bullets.body: 10-year yields at 4.65-4.66% with real yields across major economies at decade highs. The rates repricing is lifting financials laggards including FISV, FIS, and FOUR, while the 2s10s curve steepener from 29bps (June 30) to 52bps creates the most investable curve environment in years. Hyperscaler debt issuance (Amazon, Alphabet) is also distorting global high-quality credit curves.

bullets.title: Trump Imposes 100% Drone Tariffs; Commerce Gets Discretionary Authority
bullets.body: Trump signed a proclamation imposing 100% tariffs on UAS docking stations and certain critical components (including vehicles >25kg) to strengthen US supply chains. The proclamation structure is more complex than headlines suggest, with the Secretary of Commerce gaining new discretionary authority. Unusual Machines and domestic drone suppliers rallied on the news.

bullets.title: AI User Margin Advantage Broadening Beyond Tech Across S&P Sectors
bullets.body: Through Q2 earnings, companies classified as AI Users are outpacing non-AI Users on NTM margin estimates, with the advantage now broadening beyond Technology into Financials, Utilities, Discretionary, and Industrials. S&P 500 profit margins are at all-time highs; 122 S&P 500 companies have rising forward EPS estimates.

bullets.title: RDDT Joining S&P 500 on August 18; Pershing Square Discloses Six New Holdings Including NFLX
bullets.body: Reddit (RDDT) surged ~10-15% in premarket on announcement it will join the S&P 500 on August 18. Separately, Pershing Square Inc. disclosed six new investments including NFLX, SPGI, ICE, ALC, MA, and V. Bill Ackman fully exited his Hertz Global stake.

bullets.title: Hedgeye: Short USD / Long EM Thesis; Engineered Dollar Weakness Via US-Japan Intervention
bullets.body: Hedgeye's Q3 macro theme centers on engineered dollar weakness via coordinated US Treasury-Japan intervention in July. The Fed under Warsh maintains a hawkish bias with a rate hike still theoretically on the table. A soft dollar lowers funding costs for Brazil, Colombia, and the Philippines as EM expressions of the trade. The macro regime has seen an atypical frequency of quad pivots in 2026 (QUAD1→3→2→4→1→4 across Feb-Aug).

bullets.title: Jackson Hole Approaching; FX Vol Low, Carry Trades Evaluated for Attractiveness
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley podcast flags that FX volatility is currently low and the USD has lacked a strong trend, making carry trades attractive ahead of Jackson Hole and upcoming central bank decisions. Client feedback from Asia is cautious but constructive on carry. The VIX expiration next week could free up volatility.

bullets.title: Apple App Store Control Weakens; iPhone 18 Price Hikes Expected Despite Lower Costs
bullets.body: The Supreme Court denied Apple's stay request on the App Store commission ruling, making alternative app stores and side-loading increasingly likely; Apple's 15% fee on out-of-store purchases may be unenforceable. Despite negotiating lower OLED display costs ($68 vs. $110-120 for Pro Max), Apple is expected to raise iPhone 18 prices by $100-300. Apple also partnered with Alibaba to develop and train an LLM targeting the China market, shifting from its prior third-party model strategy.
